verdict.rationale: NVIDIA docs claim a second-gen FP8 Transformer Engine for LLM inference/prototyping and market the card for 'agentic AI' workloads (docs-21, docs-23), and community reports show real inference throughput being achieved (41k tok/s across cards) (comm-1). However, no named serving-stack support (TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, ROCm, llama.cpp) or FP4 evidence is given, and a technical community comment explicitly notes the RTX PRO 6000's SM120 architecture lacks tmem/tcgen05 support and that 'main libraries' are focusing on datacenter SM100/B300 parts instead, a concrete counter to the general 'documented inference story' claim (comm-4). missing for 10: explicit named serving-stack support (TensorRT-LLM/vLLM/ROCm/llama.cpp), FP4 format documentation, and resolution of the SM120 library-support gap.
